badges.JUDGMENT: our read, rule-driven from feeds since 2026-09-07
badges.MEASURED: a number someone else published, quoted with date

1.plain: Three of four sides are past their boiling points; nobody is near 100° (capitulation).
1.trade: Brent bid; 30-yr yield bid; Polymarket 'ceasefire by Oct 31' looks rich above 25%.

2.plain: Most likely next 14 days: Iran seizes a tanker; a Gulf energy strike is the second card.
2.trade: Tanker rates and war-risk premia up; XLE over SPX; long-dated Brent calls cheap if force-scenario odds are right.

3.plain: Iran wants to force an escalation before Nov 3; the US wants to squeeze and hold.
3.trade: No deal premium: fade rallies on 'talks' headlines unless a convoy actually transits.

4.plain: The door is shut: 4 ships a day.
4.trade: Each week under 10 transits/day has lifted Brent; creditor selling steepens the curve.

5.plain: Every Iranian blow now gets a US answer within a day; the ladder has climbed from ship attacks to fire on US warships.
5.trade: Response lag under 2 days = escalation risk premium; Brent call skew richer; watch for the first rung-9 act since February.

6.plain: America's quiet bill: gas, yields, rial.
6.trade: DXY firm short-term (safe haven), soft long-term (reserve share).

7.plain: Iran and the small Gulf states pay; Israel doesn't.
7.trade: Qatar and Kuwait sovereign spreads wider; Israeli equities unaffected.

8.plain: The engine (lobby, arms, oil) still beats the brake (voters) — but the gap is closing.
8.trade: LMT/RTX hold while engine ≥8; first brake-over-engine print is the sell signal.

9.plain: Stuck 30%, Bigger war 28%, Strait regime 14%, Signed deal 10%.
9.trade: Bigger-war above 30% is the level to hedge with long-dated Brent calls; Signed deal above 20% is the level for Brent < $85.

10.plain: Russia and Egypt win; Asia's importers lose; creditors trim.
10.trade: Long RUB oil revenue proxies; short INR/JPY on oil-import stress.

11.plain: Carriers hold outside Iran's 300 km ring; the fight is inside it.
11.trade: A carrier inside the ring is the tell for a wider war.

12.plain: Weak signals: watch Bushehr and Bahrain.

tiles.counter: the degree scale is our 0–10 pressure score × 10: 100° = capitulation (a side gives up its aim); each side's boiling point (68° / 66° / 70° / 70°) is where it starts acting against its own interest; the gap between boiling and 100° is how much punishment it can absorb before it folds. Small Gulf and Saudi–UAE are separate pots; the 'forced escalation' base case is Sam's judgment (prior 0.42) — falsified if no Iranian kinetic act by Oct 15
tiles.moves: a strike on US forces, a tanker seizure, a talks contact, gas above $4.30 or below $3.80
tiles.source: rules/latest pots components
tiles.trade: Brent: pressure ≥7 on all three pots has coincided with +8–12% moves inside 2 weeks (Mar, Jul); if any pot drops below its line, expect Brent −5%

tiles.counter: definitions: Stuck = no signed deal, no regime change, door under 30 ships/day, fighting continues; Signed deal = a signed US–Iran agreement (not an MOU, not a pause); Regime change = any leadership change in Tehran, including an IRGC takeover or Khamenei succession; Bigger war = US or Israeli strikes on Iranian territory sustained over a week, or a Gulf-wide exchange, or US ground forces engaged; Strait regime = passage resumes ≥30 ships/day under Iran–Oman rules or fees, no war, no signed deal; Other = anything else (Houthi Red Sea closure, US unilateral pause, etc.)
tiles.source: transfer rule from pots to five endings (rules/latest.endings)

tiles.source: TIC via FRED FORTREASPOS (Japan 42609, China 41408, Cayman 36137, UK 13005), all maturities at market value, monthly; long-term-only FORLTTREASPOS for the bills split. Since-May = change from the end-April level; since-war = change from end-February.
tiles.counter: Custodial data: Cayman is hedge funds and Belgium/Luxembourg/UK hold for others (some of it China). Market value, so part of each move is price, not sales — the June bill sell-off is real, the long-bond marks are partly the yield rise. Six-week lag; July lands Sep 17 and can rewrite the ranking.
tiles.moves: TIC monthly ~17th (July on Sep 17); ranking re-run each month from the same four series plus Norway and Saudi as challengers
tiles.trade: Bills are what an FX-intervention seller dumps: a rising Japanese bill sale with a falling yen is the tell for the next intervention; the 30-yr reacts to China and Cayman, not Japan

tiles.source: Federal Reserve H.4.1, memorandum item: marketable Treasury securities held in custody for foreign official and international accounts (FRED WMTSECL1), Wednesday level, published Thursday 16:30 ET. Weekly since Apr 29 2026.
tiles.counter: Covers official accounts only (central banks, sovereign funds), not hedge funds or UK banks, and only what is custodied at the New York Fed — a central bank moving paper to Euroclear shows as a sale here without selling. It is a market-value level, so yields move it too. No public source gives daily per-country holdings; this is the closest weekly proxy.
tiles.moves: Every Thursday evening: append the new Wednesday level (the 19:00 run); a weekly drop above $30B is the alert line; cross-check with Japan MoF weekly securities flows (Thursday) when available
tiles.trade: Custody −$134B since end-April with the 30-yr at a 20-year high = official selling into a bear-steepener; a week of +$30B or more after an intervention has marked the local top in yields twice (Jul 29, Aug 26)

tiles.source: GDP and revenue numbers from press; ranking is ours

tiles.counter: AIS shows only ships that broadcast — dark tankers and most warships are invisible; ADS-B shows only aircraft with transponders on — military aircraft over Iran do not broadcast, so an empty sky is 'not seen', not 'not there'. Dead-reckoned positions are extrapolations, not fixes. Thermal anomalies cannot say what burned or who lit it
tiles.source: Live layer: every AIS commercial ship from hormuz.data-tracking.net /api/ships (MarineTraffic feeds, 30-min polls) and every ADS-B aircraft from adsb.lol (four 250-nm circles) — rebuilt every 10 minutes by a GitHub Action (live.json) and, between fixes, moved along last course and speed (dead reckoning, ≤20 min). Basemap: NASA VIIRS true colour via GIBS, newest complete pass (date on the toggle). Fire dots: VIIRS 375 m thermal anomalies, last 48 h (flares are normal; a new dot at a port, refinery or base is the signal). US warship positions: USNI Fleet Tracker / CENTCOM, approximate (JUDGMENT) · Satellite checks (S badges): Sentinel-2 via GIBS, 30 m, latest cloud-free pass per site, vessel counts at pier/anchor are our reading (JUDGMENT)

Scoreboard = latest official prints, not forecasts: Rosstat Q2 GDP (Aug 12), Bank of Russia balance of payments (Jan–May goods surplus, Q2 current account), MinFin monthly oil & gas revenue and H1 deficit; China NBS Q2 GDP / Jul activity / PPI-CPI (Aug 17) and General Administration of Customs August trade (Sep 8); Korea MOTIE August trade (Sep 1), Bank of Korea Q2 advance GDP and GDI, KRX H1 operating profit, SK hynix 2Q26; Brazil IBGE Q2 GDP, MDIC monthly trade, BCB Focus survey; Malaysia DOSM July trade (Aug 20), MITI, IMF WEO Jul 2026 for the growth forecast. Export-engine bars: same customs/ministry releases; Russia surplus = Jan–May monthly average; ringgit at 4.2 RM/$.
tiles.counter: These are correlations with the war window, not attributions: Korea and Malaysia are riding the AI-chip cycle, China's record exports are partly tariff front-running and a weak yuan, Brazil's crude surge started before March. Russia's beat is Q2 y/y against a weak 2025 base and its budget oil take is still falling. Most trade prints are one month; Q2 GDP is preliminary and gets revised.
tiles.moves: Monthly: China customs (~7th), Korea MOTIE (1st), Brazil MDIC (1st week), Malaysia DOSM (~20th), Russian MinFin oil & gas revenue (3rd). Quarterly: Q3 GDP prints late Oct (Korea, China) and Nov (Russia, Brazil). IMF October WEO replaces the July forecast column.
tiles.trade: The trade is not Russia or China — it is the AI-hardware exporters (Korea, Malaysia, Taiwan) and non-Gulf crude exporters (Brazil) that carry a war premium without war exposure; China gets export volume but no domestic lift; Russia gets prices and a current-account cushion but not budget cash.
